design: Pure re-analysis, no retrieval issued. The hybrid run over the 332 anchored targets is paired against the already-measured semantic run over the identical 332 targets, both at depth 50. Its purpose is to establish whether the anchored subset is simply the easier one.
disclosures: A declined hybrid query is scored as a complete miss, which is how declines are treated throughout this evaluation.

The 332 anchored targets are selected by the availability of a term meeting the anchor rule rather than at random, so the hybrid figure is conditional on that availability. The paired semantic column is what makes the subset auditable: it shows how the same targets behave for a mode that needs no anchor at all.
Both arms are drawn from runs already reported, and the extraction is asserted to reproduce both published summaries before any comparison is computed, so this file cannot disagree with them.

The two modes are not independent: the hybrid mode is the semantic mode with an additional set-membership predicate, so a paired test here measures what the predicate adds rather than comparing two unrelated systems.
verdict: On the identical 332 targets the hybrid mode reaches Hit@10 0.9277 against the semantic mode's 0.6717 (88 wins, 3 losses). Anchor availability tracks semantic difficulty: semantic Hit@10 is 0.6717 on anchored targets against 0.6071 on unanchored ones, a gap of 0.0646.
